title: First hour on ISD
subtitle: Login, $HOME, then compile something — the distro, not the kernel
what_you_see: First-boot asks for a user, then a getty, then a prompt in your home. tcc will compile a file you own.
why_it_matters: ISD is the product you boot: rootfs, runit, accounts, /home. IR0 only supplies the syscalls. No ISD logo yet — the machine is the brand.

dual_view.user:
firstboot → login
$ pwd
/home/ivan
$ tcc -o hello hello.c
dual_view.kernel:
runit PID 1
  ↓ getty / ash
  ↓ MINIX /home
  ↓ exec tcc (ISD package)

steps.label: First-boot account
steps.what_ir0_does: ir0_firstboot prompts for username/hostname/password (or a seed in the lab). Markers: /var/lib/ir0/firstboot.done.
steps.why_it_matters: No implicit account on a real TTY. The distro creates the user; the kernel does not.

steps.label: Login shell
steps.what_ir0_does: getty then ash. You have a prompt. $HOME is /home/<user> on the MINIX rootfs.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the same prompt Boot IR0 ends on — now it is yours.

steps.label: Compile in $HOME
steps.what_ir0_does: Guest TCC (ISD package) reads your .c via open/read, writes an ELF, execve runs it.
steps.why_it_matters: The first hour ends when you can build something on the box, not when the kernel printed a banner.
